newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends weaker as Dec/March widens.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends weaker as Dec/March widens.

text.p: London cocoa futures on Thursday shed some of their gains made earlier this week in a move that seemed to traders to be merely consolidation.
London's focus remained strictly on the Dec/March structure which widened to 47 stg at the close. The contract will enter its expiry period on Monday.

Traders said December's frailty was due to perceptions that spot cocoa would have a short validity. Stacks of cocoa graded earlier this year as part of a squeeze in September will have to be re-graded after December.
Long liquidation was also cited as another factor.
Benchmark March cocoa ended at its midday level of 929 stg a tonne, down 11 stg on the day and just off the session low of 927. December lost 20 stg to end at 881 stg.
Turnover totalled a moderate 5,480 lots which traders said was mostly taken up by Dec/March switches.
"If you take Dec/March, there is nothing else," said one trader.
December's open interest continued to shrink -- the uncovereds stood at 4,637 lots on Wednesday -- but traders expected a reasonable delivery.
Technically, 924 stg could provide mild support for March but the downside target is the gap between 917 and 913.
Market sources said Ivorian arrivals in the next few weeks could set the direction as traders seek clues on the extent of the 1996/97 crop to forecast the possible size of the production deficit.
